name: Bionic contact lens

lead: A bionic contact lens embeds tiny circuits, LEDs, sensors and an antenna into a soft lens. The aim is overlays on the wearer's view and tear-fluid monitoring, built into an accessory worn on the eye.
Its link to looks is as a future eye accessory rather than a cosmetic effect today. A University of Washington prototype in 2008 had a one-pixel LED and was tested in rabbits.

paras: Not available as a consumer product; development is by research groups and companies.
Challenges include power, biocompatibility and oxygen permeability.

angle.text: Developers aim at displays and health sensing in an eye-worn device. Its connection to looks is as a prospective eye accessory.

lead: A bionic contact lens is a thin, flexible lens that embeds microelectronics such as LEDs, circuits, sensors and antennas to display information or monitor the eye [1]. The concept was demonstrated in 2008 at the University of Washington under Babak Parviz, with a one-pixel red LED powered wirelessly and tested in rabbits for up to 20 minutes [1].

Companies including Mojo Vision and Innovega have pursued AR lens systems; Mojo pivoted in 2023 towards licensing microLED platforms [1]. Wikipedia calls the device a proposed one, with wireless power as an expected development [2].
No clinical studies of consumer use for appearance exist.

paras: Components include microLED arrays, tear sensors for glucose or intraocular pressure, microprocessors and antennas for wireless power and data [1].
No studies found for appearance use. Early prototypes were safety tested in rabbits [2].

timeline.event: Mojo Vision pivots to microLED licensing [1].
